questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A spring of force constant k is cut into two equal halves. The force constant of each half becomes:
questions.explanation: Force constant varies inversely with length, so halving the length doubles k. A shorter spring is therefore stiffer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The value of acceleration due to gravity is minimum at:
options: It is the same everywhere on Earth
questions.explanation: The Earth bulges at the equator, so the radius is largest there, and the rotational effect further reduces the effective value of g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The energy stored in a capacitor of capacitance C charged to a potential difference V is:
questions.explanation: Energy builds up as charge is added against a rising potential, giving U = ½CV² = ½QV = Q²/2C.
questions.ncertReference: Physics Class 12, Chapter 2: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to VSEPR theory, the shape of the ammonia molecule is:
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has three bond pairs and one lone pair in a tetrahedral arrangement, but the shape counts only the atoms, so it is pyramidal with a bond angle of about 107°.
questions.ncertReference: Chemistry Class 11, Chapter 4: Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: According to Faraday's first law of electrolysis, the mass of a substance deposited at an electrode is proportional to:
questions.explanation: m = ZIt, where Q = It is the total charge passed. One faraday, 96500 C, deposits one gram equivalent of the substance.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question: The IUPAC name of the complex [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] is:
questions.explanation: Ligands are named alphabetically (ammine before chlorido) before the metal, and the complex is neutral so the metal keeps its own name rather than the -ate ending. Platinum here is +2.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: Which simple permanent tissue provides mechanical strength to young stems and the petioles of leaves while still allowing them to grow?
questions.explanation: Collenchyma cells are living, with cellulose and pectin thickened at the corners, so they give flexible support. Sclerenchyma is dead and rigid.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 6: Anatomy of Flowering Plants

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question: The relationship between a fig tree and its specific pollinator wasp species is an example of:
questions.explanation: The wasp pollinates the fig and in return uses some developing seeds to raise its larvae, so both partners benefit and neither can reproduce without the other.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 12, Chapter 11: Organisms and Populations

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Which type of epithelial tissue lines the inner surface of the small intestine and helps in absorption?
questions.explanation: Tall columnar cells, often with microvilli, increase the absorptive surface. Simple squamous lines alveoli for diffusion and stratified squamous protects the skin.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 7: Structural Organisation in Animals

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question: Excess secretion of growth hormone in an adult, after the epiphyseal plates have closed, causes:
questions.explanation: Long bones can no longer lengthen, so the hands, feet and jaw thicken instead. The same excess before puberty would cause gigantism.
questions.ncertReference: Biology Class 11, Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration
